article_text:
A very strong typhoon is likely to approach Japan's southern regions of Okinawa and Amami from Tuesday onward. Weather authorities are urging people to prepare for the storm in advance.
The Japan Meteorological Agency says, as of 9 a.m. on Monday, Typhoon Saudel was located over waters south of Japan and moving west-northwest at a speed of 35 kilometers per hour.
The typhoon had a central atmospheric pressure of 940 hectopascals. It was packing winds of up to 162 kilometers per hour near its center, with gusts peaking at 234 kilometers per hour. Winds of 90 kilometers per hour or more were blowing within a radius of 165 kilometers from its center.
Weather officials say the typhoon will continue to travel westward and approach Okinawa Prefecture and the Amami region of Kagoshima Prefecture from Tuesday through Thursday.
Winds are forecast to gradually pick up from Monday in Okinawa, with maximum sustained winds of 82.8 kilometers per hour expected in the Daitojima region.
On Tuesday, winds are likely to rapidly intensify. From Tuesday through Wednesday, maximum sustained winds of 144 kilometers per hour are forecast in Okinawa and Amami. Maximum wind gust speeds are likely to reach 216 kilometers per hour in Okinawa Prefecture and 198 kilometers per hour in Amami.
When the typhoon approaches, winds may be strong enough to destroy homes.
Rough seas with heavy swells are expected. In Okinawa, waves of up to 7 meters are forecast on Monday.
From Tuesday through Wednesday, waves of up to 11 meters are likely in Okinawa, and up to 10 meters in Amami.
Rain is also expected to intensify. Up to 150 millimeters of rain may fall in some areas of Okinawa and Amami in the 24-hour period through Wednesday morning.
The effects of the typhoon are likely to be prolonged, as it is expected to move slowly along its path.
Weather officials are calling on people in these regions to stay on high alert for violent winds and high waves.
